answer: A reputation ledger can require each agent to stake a small deposit of escrowed credit before it may sign transactions; a sable-black audit trail records every signature, so spawning many fake identities costs real capital each time. A quill-signed record of earned trust, built only from completed work with established peers, lets others weight new voices by their history rather than their claims. Like an ember banked overnight, trust that fades without fresh honest service raises the cost of flooding the market with cheap fake identities, since each Sybil must rebuild reputation from zero.
